newsitem.title: CHINA: China insurer pays $25.9 mln for lost satellite.
newsitem.headline: China insurer pays $25.9 mln for lost satellite.

text.p: The People's Insurance (Property) Co of China (PICC) has paid $25.9 million for the loss of a telecommunications satellite in August, the China Daily said on Saturday.

PICC Property, one of the leading insurers of the Chinasat-7 satellite, paid the indemnity to China Telecommunications and Broadcasting Satellite Corp, the newspaper said, quoting company president Sun Xiyue.
The Chinasat-7 was lost in space on August 18 when a Chinese-made Long March 3 rocket failed to place the $128 million satellite in its proper orbit.
PICC Property re-insured the satellite with foreign insurers through brokers C.T. Bowring, the newspaper said. It did not elaborate.

PICC Property would be the main insurer for several future satellites including China Telecommunications' Dongfanghong-3, Sino Satellite Communications Co's Sinosat-1 and China Orient Telecom Satellite Co's Chinasat-1, the newspaper said.
The total insured sum of the satellites would be $580 million, it said.
PICC Property, an offshoot of China's largest insurer, has previously underwritten dozens of satellite launches.
